what_its_for: Nevirapine is an antiviral medicine used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection in adults and children. It belongs to a group of medicines called non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). It helps lower the amount of HIV in your body, keeps your immune system stronger, and lowers your risk of getting infections related to HIV. It does NOT cure HIV, but it helps control it.
how_to_take: Take nevirapine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the extended-release tablet (Viramune XR) whole — do NOT crush, chew, or split it. The regular tablet can be cut or crushed if needed. Never take nevirapine alone — it must always be used with at least two other HIV medicines. Do not skip doses or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as this can make the virus harder to treat.
dosing: For adults starting nevirapine for the first time, the usual dose is one 200 mg regular tablet once a day for the first 14 days (this is called the 'lead-in' period). After 14 days, if you have no rash or liver problems, your doctor will increase your dose to 200 mg twice a day (regular tablet) OR switch you to one 400 mg extended-release tablet (Viramune XR) once a day. For children, the dose is based on body weight and age — your doctor will calculate the right dose. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you miss doses often, talk to your doctor or pharmacist for tips to help you remember.
storage: Store nevirapine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine past its expiration date. Dispose of unused medicine properly — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking nevirapine with rifampin (a TB medicine), ketoconazole, or St. John's Wort, as these can make nevirapine less effective or cause serious side effects. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase liver damage risk. Do not share this medicine with others. Nevirapine does NOT prevent passing HIV to others through sex or blood — continue to use safe sex practices and avoid sharing needles.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor RIGHT AWAY or go to the emergency room if you notice: a skin rash (especially in the first 18 weeks of treatment), blisters, peeling skin, or sores in your mouth; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or pale-colored stools; severe tiredness or stomach pain; nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite that is severe; fever, chills, or flu-like symptoms; muscle aches or joint pain; or any signs of a severe allergic reaction such as difficulty breathing or swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Do NOT restart nevirapine on your own if you had to stop due to a rash — call your doctor first.
when_it_works: Nevirapine starts working within a few days to weeks, but it may take several weeks to months before you feel the full benefit. Regular blood tests (viral load and CD4 count) will show your doctor how well the medicine is working. Even if you feel well, keep taking your medicine every day as prescribed — stopping can allow the virus to multiply and become resistant to treatment.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Nevirapine can be used during pregnancy to help prevent passing HIV to your baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Liver disease: Use with caution if you have liver problems. Nevirapine can cause serious liver damage — your doctor will monitor your liver closely, especially in the first 18 weeks. Women with higher CD4 counts (above 250 cells/mm³) and men with CD4 counts above 400 cells/mm³ have a higher risk of liver side effects. Kidney disease: Nevirapine does not usually require a dose change for kidney problems, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Children: This medicine can be used in children from birth onward with careful dosing based on weight. Elderly patients: Use with caution; your doctor will monitor you closely for any side effects.
